ai.title: Enforce deterministic writefile content
ai.summary: write_file now requires complete file content, removing edit snippet support. Placeholder comment logic and fastRewrite dependencies deleted from common/src/util/string.ts and packages/agent-runtime/src/fast-rewrite.ts. Scope covers agent types, editor prompts, and tool params in common/src/tools/params/tool/write-file.ts. Models must output full files; lazy edits like '// ... existing code ...' are no longer parsed.

eli5.text: The agent can no longer save just a small edit to a file; it must now produce the entire file content every time it writes. This means lazy shortcuts like leaving placeholder comments (e.g., //... existing code...) to stand in for unchanged parts of code are no longer accepted, the system treats them as the literal text they wrote. This makes every save fully deterministic: what the agent outputs is exactly what lands on disk, with no behind-the-scenes guessing or stitching of snippets. It is live today and applies to all agent types that write files.

ai.title: Refactor prompt cache tests to use real API and git status checks
ai.summary: Replaced mocked prompt cache tests with real integration tests using CodebuffClient and API key. Added test case verifying cache validity despite git status changes between requests. Requires CODEBUFF_API_KEY environment variable; skips gracefully if missing.

eli5.text: The test that checks whether reusing a previous conversation makes the assistant cheaper to run has been rewritten so it now talks to the real online service instead of a pretend stand-in, and it also confirms that simply having files change on your computer between requests does not wipe out that savings. You, as someone running these tests, will now need an API key set up as a secret environment variable for the test to actually run; if you do not have one, the test quietly skips itself instead of failing. When you do run it, you should see two real cost figures printed in the logs instead of the fake ones used before.
